projects.tagline: Tenant isolation, role-based access and document workflows with a full audit trail.
projects.solutionOverview: Multi-tenant application with subdomain isolation, a permission model across six roles and a document workflow covering upload, classification, signature and archival. Delivered as a container image and operated on cloud infrastructure.
projects.businessProblem: Processes running on paper and shared drives, with no traceability and no way to prove who approved what.
projects.role: Solution architecture, data model, API design and front-end delivery, plus ownership of the deployment pipeline and production operations.
projects.description: Reference implementation of the architecture patterns the team reuses today.
projects.callToAction: Happy to walk through the data model, the isolation strategy and the trade-offs behind them.

impact.ops: Manual handling of documents removed from the daily workflow
impact.quality: Every state change leaves an auditable trail
impact.scalability: New tenants are provisioned without code changes

technicalDecisions: Tenant isolation enforced in the data layer with a global filter, instead of trusting every query to remember it.
Immutable history for document state changes: the audit trail is built from events, not from mutable rows.
Container images built once in CI and promoted between environments, so what is tested is what runs.
technicalChallenges: Keeping read performance acceptable with tenant filters applied to every query.
Modelling signatures with three assurance levels without duplicating the workflow.

projects.tagline: Images built in CI, published to a registry and deployed with health-checked rollback.
projects.solutionOverview: Multi-architecture images built and pushed to the GitHub Container Registry (GHCR), then released with Docker Compose behind a reverse proxy. Every release verifies service health before switching traffic and reverts automatically when the check fails.
projects.businessProblem: Releases that needed a maintenance window, a manual checklist and a rollback plan agreed in a chat message.
projects.role: Pipeline design and implementation, plus the operational runbook and the rollback criteria.
projects.description: The deployment path every project in this portfolio now follows.
projects.callToAction: Can show the pipeline definition and the rollback behaviour end to end.

impact.ops: Releases no longer need a maintenance window
impact.quality: A failed health check reverts before it reaches users
impact.scalability: The same pipeline serves every project

metrics: Automatic revert on failed health check
technicalDecisions: Immutable images tagged by commit and promoted between environments instead of rebuilt.
The health check is the release gate: no traffic switch until the service answers correctly.
Pre-flight backups and controlled migrations, so a revert never needs a manual database fix.
technicalChallenges: Getting multi-architecture builds to cache well enough to stay under a few minutes.
Making rollback safe once a migration has already run.

projects.tagline: Live operational dashboards with combinable filters and scheduled exports.
projects.solutionOverview: Push-based dashboards over a signal channel, aggregations computed in the database and exports scheduled to spreadsheet and PDF. Designed to stay readable on always-on screens.
projects.businessProblem: Teams making decisions from a spreadsheet that was already hours out of date.
projects.role: Data model, aggregation strategy, front-end implementation and the export jobs.
projects.description: Where most of the reporting experience in this portfolio comes from.
projects.callToAction: Available to discuss aggregation strategy and how to keep dashboards honest.

impact.ops: Decisions made on live numbers instead of yesterday's file
impact.quality: One definition per metric, shared by every view
impact.scalability: New panels reuse the same aggregation layer

metrics: Sub-second updates on the operational view
technicalDecisions: Aggregations computed in the database and cached by time bucket, not in the browser.
Push updates limited to the visible time window, to avoid flooding the client.
Exports generated by the same code path as the on-screen view, so the numbers always match.
technicalChallenges: Keeping the interface responsive with several panels subscribing at once.
Reconciling timezone boundaries between the operational view and the stored history.
